verdict.rationale: Milvus ships Milvus Lite, a local file-backed instance for prototyping that shares the same API and client code as Standalone and Distributed. A user can therefore test against an isolated local database and use the same code in production. However, this is a separate lightweight deployment rather than a documented sandbox or staging feature, and Lite covers only 'most' features. missing for 10: an explicit sandbox/test-environment feature, documented isolation guarantees from production data, a way to seed or clone test data from production safely, full feature parity, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: To create a local Milvus vector database, simply instantiate a `MilvusClient` by specifying a file name to store all data

With the same client-side code, you can run GenAI apps with Milvus Lite on a laptop or Jupyter Notebook, or Milvus Standalone on Docker container, or Milvus Distributed on massive scale Kubernetes cluster serving billions of vectors in production.
Milvus Lite shares the same API with Milvus Standalone and Distributed, and covers most of the features
it’s ideal for quick prototyping in Jupyter Notebooks or running on edge devices
